doc.title: Albert Warner and Sonny Henry Interview, 1959-01-08

chapter: Eureka Brass Band and Sonny Henry
title: Reading versus faking
summary: Allen reassures them about the tapes; Sonny Henry and Warner argue that a musician must both read and fake.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Look, don't be afraid what you're going to say. We can save these tapes and not play them for anybody. I say this is for a hundred years from now. You know, if you want to, we can put like a restriction on it, they call it, you know, and not to be played for ten years, you know, or something. So don't worry, just speak your mind.
Sure. You know what I mean? That's all you can do, you don't think you need to know. You see, Jim, just like you always say about Jim. Jim, he's my friend.
Yeah, we all know that. We know your buddies, yeah.

Yeah, but they all, sometimes some guy, oh, did Jim beat you? I say, yeah. Yeah, yeah, Jim, do Jim know more than you? I say, yeah, I don't tell him, I don't tell him. I say, good. I say, I say, I say, but there's one thing. I say, Jim, he makes a living more of a chair than I have. I have made my living more of a chair too. I say, well, what, what, what use for me knocking Jim? You understand? Well, when I've come along, I, I did good. Mm-hmm. You mean he might come up? But, and then this is the question I asked him. I said, sir, if a man go to school, I said, understand me very well. You don't go to school. I said, if a newspaper, if I can take a newspaper and read it and you can't read it. I said, who is the most best man? The question has not been answered as yet with me, with the first one. Oh, he can do it, but I said, answer my question. As yet, it has not been answered as yet.
In other words, if he get a check, he put a cross mark and you can sign your name, well there's a big difference in it.
Well, he didn't sign at this. You see, he's all right in his style of things.
Don't let him want to feel it.

You can play with fellas that can use you in those things. Me too. I like his playing. You go get with some other bands, like Up The Line. Now, you know when you go up the line, that routine's all right, but they want you to see too. Yeah. You can only say, I'm a trombone player, you see, and I can play. All right, now when you say you can play, they're going to get that music, they're going to put it there. All right, now what you're going to do? You're going to wait until somebody started playing? Well, that man ain't waiting until somebody else started playing, he won't see what you're doing. See? And you can't fool them people. They, they, when they, you see it all the time, we get up and you read that musician, this book there. Uh-huh. They sometimes calling for men. They want a man that can fake and read too. You got to do both. Yeah. Well, how the hell are they going to do? You can't, you do your, if you can fake and you can't read, well they can't use you. You can get out there and play with these fellas that, that know that you just can fake, well then they're going to let you go by with that. See? But if they ever get any place where they got the, all of them do some reading themselves, well then that's where you at. Don't pee then. You're handicapped. You're just like a crippled child.
